HF.name: hydrogen fluoride
HF.fact: Hydrogen shares one pair with fluorine. Fluorine then has 2 + 6 = 8 electrons (an octet) and hydrogen has 2 (a duet).

H2O.name: water
H2O.fact: Oxygen has 6 valence electrons: 4 of them make two lone pairs and 2 are shared in the two O–H bonds. A Lewis diagram is flat; the real molecule is bent.

NH3.name: ammonia
NH3.fact: Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons: 3 are shared in N–H bonds and 2 stay as one lone pair.

CH4.name: methane
CH4.fact: Carbon has 4 valence electrons and all 4 are shared in C–H bonds, so there are no lone pairs at all.

H2S.name: hydrogen sulfide
H2S.fact: Sulfur is in the same group as oxygen, so it also has 6 valence electrons: two lone pairs and two S–H bonds.

CO2.name: carbon dioxide
CO2.fact: Two single bonds would leave carbon with only 4 electrons. Two C=O double bonds give every atom an octet.

HCN.name: hydrogen cyanide
HCN.fact: Carbon makes one single bond to hydrogen and a triple bond to nitrogen, which keeps one lone pair.

O2.name: oxygen gas
O2.fact: Two oxygen atoms share two pairs (a double bond) and each keeps two lone pairs: 4 + 8 = 12 valence electrons.

CH2O.name: methanal (formaldehyde)
CH2O.fact: Carbon makes two single bonds to hydrogen and a double bond to oxygen, so it has three bonding regions and no lone pairs.

C2H4.name: ethene
C2H4.fact: Each carbon needs four bonds. Each makes two C–H bonds, so the two carbons share two pairs: a C=C double bond.

BF3.name: boron trifluoride
BF3.fact: Boron is an exception to the octet rule: it is happy with 6 electrons. With three bonding regions and no lone pair the shape is trigonal planar.

NF3.name: nitrogen trifluoride
NF3.fact: Nitrogen keeps a lone pair and each fluorine keeps three: 5 + 3 × 7 = 26 valence electrons in all.

CCl4.name: tetrachloromethane
CCl4.fact: Carbon forms four single bonds and each chlorine keeps three lone pairs: 4 + 4 × 7 = 32 valence electrons.

levels.title: Lone pairs
levels.subtitle: Octets with single bonds
levels.tip: Try this: the bonds are drawn for you. Drag the lone-pair chips onto the atoms until every atom has an octet (8 electrons), and hydrogen has a duet (2). Then press Check.

levels.title: Double and triple bonds
levels.subtitle: Choose the bonds too
levels.tip: Try this: first count the valence electrons. Then drag a single, double or triple bond onto each link and add lone pairs until every atom is full and no electrons are left over.

levels.title: Shapes
levels.subtitle: VSEPR: name the shape
levels.tip: Try this: count the electron regions around the central atom. A double bond is one region, and a lone pair is a region too. Regions push apart as far as they can. Drag the right shape onto the molecule.

levels.title: Glacier Summit
levels.subtitle: Boss: build it, then name its shape
levels.tip: Boss! For each molecule, build the Lewis structure and then name its shape. You have 100 seconds each, and you will not be told the electron total.
